image_description: A grey whale surfacing in calm, grey ocean waters. The whale's head and upper back are visible above the waterline, showing a distinct spout of mist from its blowholes. The skin appears dark grey with lighter mottling consistent with barnacle patches. No dorsal fin is visible, only the curve of the back leading to the tail which remains submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is consistent with a grey whale, appearing blunt and arched. A prominent spout is visible, indicating the presence of blowholes, though the holes themselves are obscured by the mist and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin shows characteristic mottling with lighter grey/white patches against a darker background, matching the description of barnacle encrustation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is clearly no dorsal fin. The back curves smoothly into the water, consistent with the dorsal knuckle structure of a grey whale, although the knuckles themselves are partially submerged or low-profile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior portion of the body is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified as the rear half is submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and underwater; baleen plates are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located on the underside/lower sides and are completely submerged in this surface view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are entirely underwater and not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin surface appears textured and uneven, consistent with the rough texture and callosities described, rather than being perfectly smooth like a dolphin.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The water ripples immediately surrounding the whale's body appear slightly smudged and lack the crisp high-frequency detail expected from a real photograph, suggesting minor AI generation smoothing or 'melting' at the boundary.

The mist from the blowhole has a somewhat uniform, painted texture rather than the complex, translucent particulate nature of real water vapor, though this could also be attributed to image resolution/compression.
